o1.biggest_strength: The bug is called out first with the money, the browser split is read properly, and the tests are ranked by expected impact with honest sample maths in plain words.
o1.biggest_mistake: The five-test schedule runs two tests at once on shared page real estate with interactio checks left late; and test 3 (firmness) is weaker and less evidenced than the firmer review-relocation idea, so one ranking slot may be soft.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tie each test tighter to one evidence line (34%, 19%, 17%, 14%, 81%) with a scannable table up front, and state the ship-rule and stop-early rules as explicitly as the lane plan.

o2.biggest_strength: Precise arithmetic on the in-app gap (23.8% vs 53.3%, 1,860 checkouts, 558 orders, ₹17-34 lakh), calendar dates, and a clear two-lane schedule with a proper ship rule.
o2.biggest_mistake: Add-to-cart as the main metric on three of five tests despite mobile converting at 0.56% and a fix that removes the reason to reach checkout; it ranks reviews above the bigger firmness doubt and the hero image as a test despite thinnest evidence.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use orders per session (or checkout reach where it fits) as the main metric wherever it pays, demote the hero image to a ship item, and write the trial and delivery lines in the brand's own words.

reason: Both get the big call right and would be usable, but Output 1 reads more like our own voice, ranks the delivery-date and size tests on the right evidence, and keeps the money and the leak front and centre; Output 2 is sharper on the bug maths but leans on add-to-cart metrics and less of our tone.
